glosses: Action given to provide assistance; aid.

examples.text: I need some help with my homework.

examples.text: He was a great help to me when I was moving house.

examples.text: I can't find anything in the help about rotating an image.

glosses: A study aid.

examples.text: I've printed out a list of math helps.

examples.text: The help is coming round this morning to clean.

examples.text: It is polite to help your guests to food before serving yourself.

examples.text: The white paint on the walls helps make the room look brighter.

glosses: To avoid; to prevent; to refrain from; to restrain (oneself). Usually used in nonassertive contexts with can.

examples.text: Are they going to beat us? Not if I can help it!

We couldn’t help but notice that you were late.

examples.text: Can you help me buy some groceries?

glosses: To save from any violence, danger or evil.

examples.text: The well-trained team rescued everyone after the avalanche.
Soon after rescuing some silly children from the local caves, the alien prangs his vessel and dies.

The students’ final mission was their longest: a trip across the Nile to the city of Omdurman, at the request of Rwandan diplomats, to rescue a woman who, unlike the first they rescued, really was pregnant.

glosses: To free or liberate from confinement or other physical restraint.

examples.text: to rescue a prisoner from the enemy

glosses: To recover forcibly, especially from a siege.
To remove or withdraw from a state of exposure to evil and sin.

examples.text: Traditionally missionaries aim to rescue many ignorant heathen souls.

glosses: To achieve something positive under difficult conditions.

examples.text: Jews rescued some normalcy from increasingly difficult times by assuaging their constant Angst in the family and community and making do with less.
Arsenal's hopes of starting their Champions League campaign with an away win were dashed when substitute Ivan Perisic's superb late volley rescued a point for Borussia Dortmund.

glosses: To restore a particular trait in an organism that was lost or altered, especially where this loss was as the consequence of some experimental manipulation.

examples.text: Mecp2^(R255X/+) [mice] developed an overweight body weight phenotype by 10 weeks age and increased liver and heart weight by 8 months age. Abnormal body, liver and heart weight in Mecp2^(R255X/+) was rescued by MECP2ᵀᵍ¹ allele.

glosses: To salvage and restore something that has been discarded.

examples.text: I rescued a set of antique dining chairs.

glosses: To fix a mistake made while preparing something, especially in cooking.

examples.text: The cook rescued the sauce after it began to curdle.

glosses: To adopt (an animal).

examples.text: We rescued a dog, Dylan, which would begin my lifelong love of animals, especially dogs.

glosses: An act or episode of rescuing, saving.

examples.text: Guests marveled that they kept making more rescues.
